newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures recover to end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures recover to end higher.

text.p: U.S. interest rate futures recovered from modest early losses to end the session slightly higher and near daily highs set late in the session.
Dealer and local buying boosted T-bond futures in the final hour of the session, sending the March bond above minor resistance and triggering buy stops above 112-05/32 to 112-6/32, traders said.
Futures had drifted upward throughout midmorning and afternoon activity, recovering from losses reached after U.S. economic data came in stronger than anticipated.
December U.S. new home sales slipped in December to 783,000 units, above the forecast rate of 745,000.
Traders also noted that talk the home sales figure could be even lower, perhaps as low as 500,000 units, had underpinned the market in recent sessions.
So when the housing number came out above forecasts, selling emerged that quickly sent bond futures lower, and below chart support near 111-28/32.
Little followthrough selling surfaced after the penetration of support, and prices then began a gradual drift upward.
"The upmove that began from 109-14/32 (in March T-bond futures) on Wednesday morning is not over yet," said Joe Plauche, analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds.

Plauche expects a move up to 112-16/32 in the next few sessions, to where the bond contract would be "in a position for some sort of corrective phase before the unemployment report," possibly moving down to 111-16/32 area, he said.
Employment data for January will be released Friday, and a rise of 237,000 jobs is expected in non-farm payroll employment, according to a Reuter survey of economists.
Traders said they expected no change in monetary policy from the Federal Open Market Committee meeting which began today.

At settlement, March T-bond futures were up 4/32 point at 112-07/32, 10-year T-notes were 2/32 higher at 109-07/32 and muni-bonds were 3/32 higher at 115-30/32. June IMM T-bills were unchanged at 94.86 and Eurodollars were also unchanged at 94.31. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
